title: Moving the curve

controls.label: Income moved from richest fifth to poorest fifth (points)

predict.q: Quintile shares: 5%, 10%, 15%, 25%, 45%. Gini **0.38**. A tax on the richest fifth pays for benefits to the poorest fifth, moving 5 percentage points of income. What happens?

options.s: The Lorenz curve moves towards the line of equality and the Gini falls
options.fb: Every point of the curve rises towards the line of equality; the Gini falls from 0.38 to 0.30.

options.s: The Lorenz curve moves away from the line of equality and the Gini rises
options.fb: Income moved from rich to poor, so the curve moves towards the line of equality, not away.

options.s: Nothing changes, because total income is the same
options.fb: Total income is the same, but its shares change; the Lorenz curve shows shares.

options.s: The Gini falls, and the line of equality moves down towards the curve
options.fb: The line of equality never moves: it is fixed at equal shares. The Lorenz curve moves.

task: Move the transfer slider to 5 and watch the curve and the Gini.

target.do: Move the transfer slider to 5, then press Check.

takeaway: Shifting income from richer to poorer groups pulls the Lorenz curve towards the line of equality; here the Gini falls from 0.38 to 0.30.
